canonical_name: compress 4.2.4 -- the earlier Unix LZW compress (ncompress lineage)
lineage: compress 4.x (1985-1992): the Unix LZW compressor as it stood before the long ncompress maintenance era; the EARLY version of the same lineage batch 01 preserved at ncompress 5.0
version: git tag v4.2.4.6, github.com/vapier/ncompress (the tagged historical 4.2.4 line)

example.command: make && ./compress -c compress.c | ./compress -dc | cmp - compress.c && echo ROUNDTRIP_OK

upstream_docs: Welch, A Technique for High-Performance Data Compression, 1984

human_capability_summary.built_to: shrink files with adaptive LZW dictionary coding -- the same job as the 5.0 version, in the earlier code, before decades of portability maintenance
human_capability_summary.pressure: 1980s bandwidth and disk; the LZW patent that eventually pushed the world to gzip
human_capability_summary.success_means: exact reconstruction; and, as a fossil PAIR with ncompress 5.0, a preserved 30-year span of the SAME lineage for later diff

lineage_relations.note: compress 4.2.4 (1992) is the earlier form; ncompress 5.0 (2021) is the later. Same LZW lineage, ~30 years apart -- the batch-03 one-specimen-many-versions pair. What changed mechanistically is Nyx's question.

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run compress-4.2.4-lzw
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: shrink files with adaptive LZW dictionary coding -- the same job as the 5.0 version, in the earlier code, before decades of portability maintenance
